source_name: BQK – Lista e institucioneve financiare të licencuara/regjistruara (Central Bank of Kosovo)
why_relevant: Complementary mandatory register: any payment institution, e-money issuer, bank, MFI or NBFI must be licensed by BQK. Cross-referencing the BQK list against ARBK registrations separates licensed payments players from unlicensed IT vendors, and dates market entry.

source_name: ASK – Agjencia e Statistikave të Kosovës (statistical business register / NACE-based economic activity statistics)
why_relevant: Aggregate counts of enterprises by NACE activity and size class (incl. J – information & communication, K – financial activities) give the denominator for interpreting registry hits, and identify the exact activity-code taxonomy used in ARBK filings.

source_name: ARBK guidance on registering a branch of a foreign company (dega e shoqërisë së huaj)
why_relevant: Defines the legal form used by foreign vendors entering Kosovo without incorporating a subsidiary, the documents filed (incorporation certificate, jurisdiction of incorporation), and hence exactly which fields of a registry record reveal a foreign parent. Reported ~1,327 foreign branches registered — a bounded, searchable population.

source_name: TheKYB – Kosovo business registry data (commercial KYB provider)
why_relevant: Commercial KYB feed claiming real-time Kosovo registry coverage; relevant as a fallback bulk-access route and as evidence of which registry fields are machine-available (status, officers, addresses).

source_name: eKosova national services portal (municipal one-stop-shop business registration pages)
why_relevant: Municipal one-stop-shop pages document the 29 local registration centres and business-type taxonomy, and occasionally publish local business listings — useful for locating vendor operations outside Prishtina.

source_name: APR Srbija – Agencija za privredne registre (unified entity search)
why_relevant: Serbian registry is the counterpart register for the many banking/payments vendors serving Kosovo from Belgrade, and for Serbia-registered entities operating in northern Kosovo. Registry-to-registry cross-checks establish whether a 'regional' vendor has a Kosovo entity at all.

Highest-traffic Albanian-language Kosovo portal; routinely carries bank press releases verbatim (product launches, card/payment services, EBRD/IFC facility signings, MoU signings with tech vendors). Because copy is often the bank's own release, vendor and product names survive intact — useful for naming who supplied what.

source_name: Telegrafi — tag page: Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës (Kosovo Banking Association)
why_relevant: Pre-filtered stream of all Telegrafi coverage mentioning the banking association — a cheap pointer feed into sector-level events, conferences and joint bank/vendor initiatives without crawling the whole portal.

The single richest Albanian-language source for procurement irregularities and disputed IT/service contracts. Investigations name contracting authority, economic operator, contract value and complaint history — i.e. de facto vendor-win records. Has covered Central Bank (BQK) tender awards and telecom/IT contracts directly.
Stable URL namespace holding Kallxo's deep contract investigations; the highest signal-to-noise entry point for procurement-scandal mining, distinct from the high-volume daily /lajm/ wire.

Kosovo's dedicated Albanian-language business/economy portal. Covers banking-sector aggregates (credit stock, NPLs, deposits, headcount per bank), new market entrants (e.g. Albanian banks targeting the Kosovo market), and digitalisation/financing themes — the closest thing to a competitor-tracking beat in local language.

Paper-of-record daily; carries service-launch and payments coverage (e.g. ISP/utility online-payment launches identifying the acquiring bank, telco eSIM/digital launches) and general economic-policy reporting. Useful for dating market events and for identifying which bank sits behind a merchant's payment rail.

High-volume portal that publishes bank-supplied product announcements almost unedited — card form-factor launches, e-banking/diaspora remittance features. These are effectively free product-roadmap disclosures for TEB, ProCredit and peers, and often the only public record of a card or channel launch.

One of the most-watched private broadcasters; its economy vertical covers signing ceremonies, large investment agreements and government-business deals, frequently with video of the signing that identifies the counterparties.

source_name: Preportr (Kosovo Center for Investigative Journalism / Çohu)
why_relevant: Specialist procurement-and-patronage investigative magazine. Publishes quantified analyses of public tenders (hundreds of millions of euros, per-authority breakdowns) including public enterprises' IT and service contracts. Highest-detail public accounting of who supplied what to Kosovo public bodies.

English-language sibling of Kallxo; republishes BIRN/Kallxo contract and conflict-of-interest investigations in translation, including bank-conduct stories (e.g. a Turkish-owned bank closing accounts in Kosovo) and tender-winning company profiles. Cheap way to read the same evidence without sq translation cost, and useful for cross-checking names/spellings.

Regional aggregation of BIRN's Kosovo output; useful as a pointer to which Kosovo investigations BIRN considers regionally significant, and to cross-border vendor stories (Serbia/Albania/North Macedonia) that touch Kosovo banking.

Politically-driven news and investigation portal; covers how political instability affects investments, large projects and donor funding — the macro context that gates bank IT capex and vendor tenders in Kosovo. Occasionally breaks contract/appointment stories ahead of the mainstream portals.

Wire agency whose copy is syndicated across Kosovo portals; its topic tags (e.g. National Council for Economy and Investment) give an early, structured view of state-level economic initiatives that later become tenders or bank-facing programmes.

Long-running mass-market Kosovo portal with a business desk; historically a fast publisher of corporate and banking announcements. Included for completeness of the Albanian-language media set; ownership and editorial line documented by Media Ownership Monitor.

Meta-source: maps who owns each Kosovo outlet and its political/commercial affiliations. Essential for weighting credibility of the media candidates in this cell — e.g. distinguishing advertorial-driven portals from independent investigative ones, and spotting when a bank's owner also owns the outlet reporting on it.

Second Albanian-language economy portal covering Kosovo; carried the World Bank Kosovo Digital Economy (KODE) project approval — the kind of donor-funded digital programme that seeds bank/fintech connectivity and vendor procurement.

source_name: Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës — news/press section (Kosovo Banking Association)
why_relevant: Not media, but the counterpart the Albanian-language press quotes constantly — publishes sector positions on e-signature in banking, digital economy, and joint bank initiatives. Anchors the actor map and explains stories that appear in Telegrafi/Ekonomia Online.

The main independent Serbian-language Kosovo outlet. Covers payment/insurance digitalisation affecting the north (e.g. launch of online insurance-payment software at border crossings) and the parallel-institutions dimension of banking and payments that Albanian-language media under-report.

source_name: Narodna banka Srbije (NBS) — press releases / media Q&A on Kosovo dinar payment operations
why_relevant: NBS is the issuer/regulator behind the dinar payment layer used in Serb-majority municipalities; its statements are the authoritative primary record of the parallel payment arrangements, the CBK ban on dinar cash, and the workaround measures. Found a concrete media-Q&A page and a formal condemnation release (id=19478) specifically on preventing dinar transport/use in Kosovo.

source_name: NBS — Payment system statistics (platni sistem / statistika)
why_relevant: Official card-issuing, transaction-volume and acceptance-network series for Serbia. Baseline for sizing the dinar/DinaCard layer that spills into Kosovo, and the comparator against CBK Kosovo payment statistics.

source_name: NBS — Naknade pružalaca platnih usluga (payment service provider fee register)
why_relevant: Machine-comparable register of every licensed Serbian payment service provider and its fee schedule — an actor map of the dinar-side PSPs (incl. Banka Poštanska štedionica) that serve Kosovo Serb clients.

source_name: Banka Poštanska štedionica a.d. Beograd — corporate site (DinaCard, platni promet)
why_relevant: The de-facto sole dinar-operating bank serving Kosovo Serb clients (branches in Serb-majority municipalities and the four prefabricated ekspoziture at Jarinje, Brnjak, Končulj, Merdare). Product pages, card schemes (DinaCard), ATM/branch network and cross-border payment pages are the primary vendor-relevant footprint.
